text:
Bobby McMann scored 29 goals last season, a year split between Toronto and Seattle. This season he has three in 20 games and none in his last 13, and it would be easy to read that as a 30-year-old who has lost his touch.

Our numbers don't see it that way. He is still getting to his chances: 2.6 expected goals on his own shots over his last ten, right on his usual rate, and 49 shots on the season. He is shooting 6.1% against a talent range that starts at 11%. The drought is the kind that usually breaks.

The harder problem is what happens around him. Seattle gets just 42% of the 5v5 expected goals with McMann on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey says he draws the other team's best players (97th percentile competition). He is still one of the fastest skaters in the league, 95th percentile top speed, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 53% of his shots coming off the rush. Watch the transition chances: that is where the first goal in weeks should come from.
headline: Bobby McMann's chances keep coming, the goals haven't
